name: Kenya
summary_text: Kenya is a dangerous destination for trans visitors. Same-sex conduct is criminalised under the colonial-era Penal Code (14 years, applies to all including tourists). Police extortion targeting trans people is documented and systemic — a trans woman was forced to pay a $50 bribe in Mombasa, and 25 trans and intersex people told CNN this kind of police harassment is "common." The Kenya Human Rights Commission's "Lives on the Line" report documented 102 evictions, 43 unlawful arrests, and mob violence (groups stripping queer people naked) over a one-year period. An LGBTQ+ activist, Edwin Chiloba, was murdered (his body found in a metal box) — though the perpetrator was sentenced to 50 years, showing enforcement can work. However, Kenya's courts have been a surprising bright spot. The High Court ruled in 2025 that a trans woman's arrest for "personation" was unconstitutional (awarding damages and ordering the government to draft a Transgender Protection Rights Bill). In May 2026, the High Court affirmed a constitutional right to legal gender recognition. The Supreme Court has upheld LGBTQ+ freedom of association, and the Court of Appeal ruled forced anal testing unconstitutional. "Thousands of gay travelers visit annually through specialized tour operators." There is no anti-discrimination law and no LGR procedure yet, but the court-ordered Transgender Protection Rights Bill is a positive trajectory.

sources.title: Country policy and information note: sexual orientation and gender identity and expression, Kenya, February 2025 (accessible) - GOV.UK
sources.claim_summary: UK Home Office CPIN on sexual orientation and gender identity and expression in Kenya (Feb 2025, updated July 2026): official country-of-origin information and assessment for asylum claims - legal position, societal treatment, state protection.

CNN As Equals investigation: how trans and intersex people survive in Kenya - 'forced to pay bribes at every step'; a young trans woman describes being arrested on a pretext by Mombasa police and held until she paid a $50 bribe; trans people use male pseudonyms for safety; police extortion is systemic.

NOTE: The Kenya Human Rights Commission report 'Lives on the Line: Violence and Discrimination Against Sexual and Gender Minorities in Kenya' (Sept 2025) returned no extractable text at fetch time (image-based PDF).

sources.title: High Court affirms legal recognition of transgender Kenyans, directs state action to protect their rights
sources.claim_summary: Kenya Human Rights Commission press release (Aug 2025): the High Court in Eldoret affirmed legal recognition of transgender Kenyans and directed the state to enact a Transgender Protection Rights Act, ruling that prisons do not protect trans people's dignity and privacy; the case arose from invasive, nonconsensual medical procedures on a trans woman (SC) during incarceration after a 'personation' arrest.

sources.title: Kenya High Court Rules Trans and Gender Diverse People Have Constitutional Right to Legal Gender Recognition — GATE | Global Action for Trans Equality
sources.claim_summary: GATE knowledge-portal article: Kenya's High Court rules there is a constitutional right to legal gender recognition - analysis of the landmark decision.
NOTE: Not retrievable at research time (HTTP 401); the underlying Reuters report (Dec 2024) covers a Kenyan man sentenced to 50 years in jail for killing an LGBTQ activist.

sources.title: Kenya | Outright International
sources.claim_summary: Outright International country overview (updated March 2026): progress largely through courts - forced anal testing ruled unconstitutional (2018, compensation awarded 2024); the Supreme Court upheld LGBTQ organisations' freedom to register (2023), followed by pushback including protests and homophobic remarks by religious and political leaders; a 2024 High Court temporary order against incitement to hatred; same-sex conduct remains criminalised and no legal gender recognition.

sources.title: Report: Why the country is a 'hell-hole' for queer Kenyans
sources.claim_summary: The Star (Sept 2025): coverage of the KHRC report 'Lives on the Line' - 682 cases of harassment documented across regions (50 sexual harassment, 100 verbal abuse); queer Kenyans face eviction, online trolling, and being waylaid by organised groups who strip and violate them; the country is 'deeply socially conservative'.

US State Department 2010 Human Rights Report for Kenya: documents the 2007-08 post-election violence (~1,150 killed), security-force abuses, mob violence, and the LGBT section noting criminalisation under the penal code and societal discrimination.
